public_health_question.v: How do 2021 suicide rates among U.S. working persons aged 16–64 years vary by industry and occupation, by sex?

ev.q: To guide suicide prevention strategies among the working-age population, CDC analyzed 2021 suicide deaths by industry and occupation.
Suicide Rates by Industry and Occupation — National Vital Statistics System, United States, 2021
CDC analyzed suicide deaths by industry and occupation in 49 states, using data from the 2021 National Vital Statistics System.
The 2021 National Vital Statistics System (NVSS) restricted-use mortality file includes 37,435 suicide decedents aged 16–64 years

equity.level_reason: Sex is the only stratifier and age bounds define the population; industry and occupation are framed as workplace exposure, not social position. Race and education appear only in a limitation.

level_alternative.reason: Occupation could be read as SES given 'risk disparities' and the cited links to low-skilled jobs and low SES; group results vs referent are reported without quantified contrasts.

equity.equity_measurement: Referent is the sex-specific total working-population rate held fixed; nonpaid, military and unclassifiable occupations (19.8% of decedents) excluded; occupation not treated as social position.

notes: Design not named; surveillance/descriptive inferred from NVSS mortality analysis. ACS population counts are denominators only and not listed as a data source. Discussion cites low-skilled jobs, low educational attainment and SES as suicide risk factors from prior literature, not tied to an SPD group here.
view_issues: Table 2 row label 'Social workers ¶' carries the elevated mark although the male rate 29.7 (18.9–44.8) is not elevated; likely a misplaced mark. Prepass 'diagnostic_accuracy' is a false hit on 'low specificity'.
